candidates.statement: For each study and investigator site, it is critical to submit the following variables associated 191 with efficacy and their variable names: 192 • Safety Population (SAFPOP) — Total number of subjects in safety population at a given 193 site by treatment arm. When a subject has transferred from one site to another, the 194 applicant should handle reporting of such subjects consistently across sites and include in 195 the define file, or the BIMO Data Review Guide when one is provided, the reporting 196 convention used. 197 • Primary Efficacy Population (EFFPOP) — Total number of subjects in the primary efficacy 198 population, as defined in the clinical study report, at a given site by treatment arm to support 199 the proposed indication in the application. The efficacy population used should be identified 200 in the define file provided for the clinsite.xpt (e.g., Full Analysis Set, Per Protocol, Intent to 201 Treat, Modified Intent to Treat). 202 • Treatment Efficacy Result One (TRTEFFR1) — The summary statistic for each primary 203 efficacy endpoint, by treatment arm at a site, based subjects in the SAFPOP. Values reported 204 in TRTEFFR1 generally reflect simple summary statistics for the primary efficacy 205 endpoint(s). The method used for deriving the TRTEFFR1, including a description of which 206 analysis datasets and associated variables are used to derive the TRTEFFR1, should be 207 described in the define file provided with the clinsite.xpt (see discussion below for examples 208 of summary statistics according to different types of efficacy endpoints). 209

Summarize discrete endpoints by an event 233 frequency (i.e., number of events), proportion of patients with an event, proportion of 234 patients responding to treatment, or similar method at the site for the given treatment. 235 • Continuous Endpoints — Endpoints based on efficacy observations that can take on an 236 infinite number of values. Summarize continuous endpoints by the mean, median, or other 237 distributional quantile of the observations at the site for the given treatment. 238 • Time-to-Event Endpoints — Endpoints where the time to occurrence of an event is the 239 primary efficacy measurement. Summarize time-to-event endpoints by two data elements: 240 the number of events that occurred (TRTEFFR1 and TRTEFFR2) and the number of 241 censored observations (CENSOR1 and CENSOR2). 242 • Other — If the primary efficacy endpoint cannot be summarized in terms of the previous 243 guidelines, a single value or multiple values with precisely defined variable interpretations 244 should be submitted as part of the dataset. 245 In all cases, the endpoint description provided in the ENDPOINT plain-text label should be 246 expressed clearly to interpret the value provided in the TRTEFFR1 and TRTEFFR2 variables. 247

candidates.statement: 27 IMPDEV Number of Important Protocol Deviations Num Integer Total number of important protocol deviations at a given site by treatment arm for subjects in the SAFPOP. A protocol deviation is any change, divergence, or departure from the study design or procedures defined in the protocol or associated investigational plans that is not implemented or intended as a systematic change. This value should include multiple deviations per subject and all major deviation types. Important deviations are those deviations that might significantly affect the completeness, accuracy, and/or reliability of the study data or that might significantly affect a subject's rights, safety, or well-being.
